newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac reaffirms French commitment to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Chirac reaffirms French commitment to Europe.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac reaffirmed on Thursday his commitment to plans for greater European integration and vowed to press ahead with reforms to modernise France.

Chirac told a New Year press reception that a single European currency was essential to put the European Union on an equal footing with the dollar and the yen and make it "the most powerful pole in tomorrow's world".
The aim was to create conditions for lasting peace in Europe and build a pillar of growth and strength, he said.
He added that Europe could not build a large single market with many different currencies.
Chirac has regularly repeated his commitment to launching a single European currency in January 1999.
He added that the enlargement of the EU was also essential to guarantee Europe the stability it needed.
He vowed not to let up in his domestic economic reform drive and also promised a major initiative this year to guarantee the independence of the much-criticised French justice system.
"We have to go right to the end," Chirac said.
"We have to press ahead in all areas," he said. "The reforms needed do not involve one, two or three initiatives but a spirit, a will."
